items.title: linXiv-web
items.text:
linXiv-web is a browser UI for linXiv. You can search arXiv, OpenAlex and Crossref, add papers to a library, tag them, group them into projects and reading lists, read and highlight their PDFs, and take notes.

It aligns with the linxiv-dev organization but has not been adopted by linXiv maintainers, and remains unofficial.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Library: a sortable table (click any column header) and one search box covering title, abstract, authors, ids, tags, indexed full text and notes. You can filter by PDF and edit metadata for many papers at once.
  • Papers: edit metadata, look it up and compare it side by side with Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex, PubMed and bioRxiv/medRxiv. Each paper has versions, tags, notes and a PDF reader with find and highlights. arXiv TeX source can be indexed for full-text search.
  • Projects and reading lists: projects export to BibTeX, Obsidian, Zotero and .lxproj, and .lxproj files import back. Reading lists have their own page.
  • Discovery: search tabs for arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref and the local library, with an advanced arXiv query builder. Add papers by arXiv id, DOI or PDF link. The home page shows RSS/Atom feeds with filter rules, and a monitor reports new arXiv versions.
  • Authors and graph: author pages, edit and merge, ORCID backfill, and a knowledge graph of papers, authors and tags.
  • Maintenance: trash, backup, import and restore of the database, PDF folder layouts (by year, journal or both) and a background full-text indexer.
  • AI (opt-in): tag suggestions, paper summaries saved as notes, metadata cleanup. See AI features.
  • MCP (opt-in): linXiv's own MCP tools over HTTP at /mcp, for any AI tool that accept MCP protocol. See MCP server.
  • Light and dark themes, zoom and density, keyboard shortcuts and sidebar page toggles.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
linXiv-web talks to linXiv through the linxiv CLI, which prints JSON for every command. A FastAPI server runs linxiv <command> as a subprocess, passing arguments as a list without a shell, and serves a React single-page app.

flowchart LR
  browser[Browser] -- HTTP --> api["FastAPI<br>/api/*, static SPA"]
  mcp[MCP client] -- "HTTP /mcp" --> api
  api -- subprocess --> cli[linxiv CLI]
  api -- stdio --> mcpsrv[linxiv-mcp]
  cli --> data[("papers.db + pdfs/")]
  mcpsrv --> data

Library reads and writes go through the CLI, with two exceptions where the CLI has no command. PDF folder layouts move files and update their stored path in papers.db directly (under the CLI lock), and the AI summary reads text from a saved PDF.

The design is to be local-only, but linXiv-web reach out to external services itself only in these cases:

  • downloads a PDF link pasted into Add Paper before importing it (public hosts only, size-capped)
  • metadata lookup queries PubMed through NCBI E-utilities (eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), bioRxiv/medRxiv through api.biorxiv.org or others
  • when AI features are switched on, AI actions send the paper's title, abstract (and, if you choose, PDF text) to the provider you configured (Unless is local). Nothing is sent until you click an AI button.

A linXiv library allows one writing process per data dir, so the server runs CLI calls one at a time behind a lock. Work that needs many calls, such as indexing the TeX source of every saved arXiv paper, runs as a background job that makes one call per paper, so other requests get the lock in between. Jobs live in memory: restarting the server stops a running job and forgets finished ones.

linxiv always writes PDFs to <data dir>/pdfs. The container makes that path a symlink to /pdfs, so the database can stay on local disk while the PDFs sit on other storage.

Like linxiv-headless, the server refuses to start on a non-loopback address without a password.

items.title: Where to start
items.text:
• To run it: Self-hosting with Docker.
  • To learn the pages: start with the Library.
  • To change server settings: Admin Server Configuration.

linXiv-web is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

items.title: AI features
items.text:
AI features are off by default. To turn them on, open Settings → AI, tick the switch, and pick a provider: Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, or an OpenAI-compatible base URL such as http://localhost:1234/v1 for LM Studio. Paste a key (local servers may not need one), Save, then click Load models, pick one, Save again and click Test connection.

Action Where What the model gets Result AI Tags paper page, Library batch panel ("AI tags") title, categories, abstract, current tags, your existing tag vocabulary up to 8 tags to tick and add AI summary paper page "Abstract only", or "Abstract + PDF text" (first 40 pages, 60k characters) summary + key points, saved as a note on request AI cleanup Edit metadata and Library batch metadata, source "AI cleanup" title, authors, journal a candidate shown as a field diff; nothing is saved until you approve

Nothing is sent to the provider until you click an AI button, and AI actions only return previews. You decide what gets saved.

items.title: How requests are made
items.text:
Every request carries a JSON Schema and a valid example reply; Settings → AI shows both. OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible servers get structured output (response_format: json_schema), which also stops "thinking" models such as Qwen from spending the whole token budget on reasoning. A server that rejects structured output is retried with the schema in the prompt only. Anthropic uses a forced tool call.

Requests time out after 90 s, or 300 s for OpenAI-compatible servers, since local models read long prompts slowly.

LINXIV_WEB_AI_ALLOWED_HOSTS limits which hosts the OpenAI-compatible base URL may use. Cloud metadata addresses are always refused. See Admin Server Configuration.

items.title: Tagging the whole library
items.text: To tag every untagged paper in one run, use the bulk AI tags script on the server.

items.title: Tagging every untagged paper with AI
items.text:
Use this after a large import, when hundreds of papers have no tags and picking them one by one in the Library batch panel would take too long. scripts/bulk-ai-tags.sh runs on the machine that hosts the linXiv-web container. It asks the AI you set up in Settings → AI for tags for every paper that has none, and adds them.

Each paper gets the same suggestions as AI Tags on the paper page: the model reads the title, categories and abstract, and is steered toward tags your library already uses. The script adds all suggested tags, as the batch panel does when you approve without unticking any, or the first few with --max-tags.

The container keeps running and the web UI stays usable. The script talks to the server over 127.0.0.1, so tags go through the server like any other edit.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• On the server: sh, curl and jq (apt install jq on Debian and Ubuntu).
  • AI turned on in Settings → AI, with a provider, key and model saved, and Test connection passing. The script uses those saved settings; it has no provider options of its own.
  • The container running with the compose file's port (127.0.0.1:8086), and the admin password set (first-run setup done, or LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH in .env).

items.title: Getting the script onto the server
items.text:
Copy it next to your docker-compose.yml:

scp scripts/bulk-ai-tags.sh server:linxiv-web/
ssh server 'chmod +x linxiv-web/bulk-ai-tags.sh'

Then, on the server:

cd linxiv-web
./bulk-ai-tags.sh --help

See which papers it will pick up first. This makes no AI calls and changes nothing:

./bulk-ai-tags.sh --dry-run

items.title: Running it
items.text:
./bulk-ai-tags.sh

The script asks for the linXiv-web password and logs in. It checks the AI connection (the same check as Test connection) and stops there if AI is off or not set up. Then it reads the full list of untagged papers and works through it one paper at a time. Every paper gets one line in the output and in the log file:

started 2026-10-13 22:15:00: 858 untagged paper(s) on http://127.0.0.1:8086
AI gemini / gemini-2.5-flash, max tags per paper: all
OK    doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2  2021/smith-rna.pdf  single-cell rna-seq, drug response, perturbation atlas (new)
NONE  local:9f3a0c1d  scans/notes.pdf  model returned no usable tags
SKIP  local:77c1e2b4  scans/blank.pdf  no title or abstract
FAIL  arXiv:2101.00001  -  (502): Gemini error 500: internal error
done: 812 tagged, 3 none, 41 skipped, 2 failed, 858 total. Log: ./bulk-ai-tags-20261013-221500.log

Each line shows the paper id, its PDF file inside the PDF folder (- when it has none) and the tags it got. (new) marks a tag that wasn't in your library before.

Status Meaning OK Tags added NONE The model answered, but every suggestion was empty, too long, or a duplicate. The paper stays untagged SKIP The paper has no title and no abstract, so it wasn't sent FAIL The AI call or the tag save failed. The message says why. When the save failed, the line lists the tags that weren't saved

The exit status is 1 when any paper fails, and 0 otherwise. NONE and SKIP don't count as failures.

Options:

Option Effect --all Also ask about papers that already have tags, not only the untagged ones. The model is told each paper's current tags and the server drops any it repeats, so only new tags are added. See Tagging papers that already have tags --max-tags N Add only the first N suggestions per paper, 1 to 8. The default adds all of them (the model is asked for 3 to 6, the server keeps at most 8) --jobs N Ask the AI about N papers at a time, 1 to 4 (default 1). See Running papers in parallel --log FILE Log location (default ./bulk-ai-tags-<date>-<time>.log) --dry-run List the untagged papers and how many would be skipped, then stop

The script talks to the server at http://127.0.0.1:8086, the port docker-compose.yml publishes, so run it on the server itself. It also works when LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE=true.

items.title: Running papers in parallel
items.text:
--jobs 2 keeps two papers in flight: while the model answers one, the next request is already waiting. The server sends both to the provider at once; only its short library steps (reading the paper, saving the tags) take turns. Every paper still gets one line in the log, but the lines from the two workers mix, so they are no longer in list order.

./bulk-ai-tags.sh --jobs 2

It only helps when the AI end can work on two requests at the same time:

  • Cloud providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic) answer parallel requests, but count each one against your rate limit. On a free tier, --jobs 2 hits 429 twice as fast. Stay at 1 if the log fills with rate-limit failures.
  • LM Studio answers parallel requests from version 0.4.0, on its llama.cpp engine (GGUF models, runtime llama.cpp v2.0.0 or later). Each loaded model has a Max Concurrent Predictions setting, which defaults to 4. To check or change it: open the model loader, turn on Manually choose model load parameters, pick the model, turn on Show advanced settings, and set Max Concurrent Predictions to at least the --jobs value. Then load the model again. Requests beyond that number wait in LM Studio's queue rather than failing. Unified KV Cache (on by default) lets the parallel requests share the context memory instead of splitting it into fixed parts.
  • Older LM Studio, or MLX models, may handle one request at a time. The second request then waits for the first. The server gives each AI answer at most 300 seconds, and the wait counts toward that, so a slow model with --jobs 2 can turn into FAIL ... (502): ... request failed (ReadTimeout) lines. Use --jobs 1 there.

Parallel requests on a local model share the same GPU, so each answer comes back slower than alone. Total time still drops when the model runs well below the GPU's limits. Time the first lines of a run with --jobs 1 and with --jobs 2 and keep the faster one.

Tags that one worker adds don't reach a paper the other worker is tagging at the same moment, so two papers on a new topic can come back with two spellings of the same tag. Look through the (new) tags afterwards.

With more than one job, a lost login (the container restarted mid-run) isn't renewed. The affected papers are logged as FAIL ... (401), and a rerun picks them up. Ctrl+C stops all workers. A paper whose tags were already on their way to the server still gets them.

items.title: Tagging papers that already have tags
items.text:
./bulk-ai-tags.sh --all --dry-run
./bulk-ai-tags.sh --all

--all lists every paper in the library, not only the untagged ones. A tagged paper keeps its tags and gets the model's additional suggestions on top. It costs one AI call per paper in the whole library, so a large library means a long run, and many paid requests with a cloud provider. Use --max-tags to limit how many tags each paper gains. A NONE line for a tagged paper means the model had nothing new to add.

Nothing remembers which papers a previous --all run already handled: running it again asks about every paper again.

items.title: Running it again
items.text:
A paper that got tags is no longer untagged, so a second run only picks up the NONE, SKIP and FAIL papers from the first one, plus anything imported since. Stopping a run with Ctrl+C is safe: the papers tagged so far keep their tags, and the next run carries on with the rest.

SKIP papers come back every run until they have a title or an abstract. Fix their metadata first (see below), or tag them by hand.

items.title: Running it without a terminal (cron)
items.text:
The script reads the password from the first line of the file named in LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_FILE. Keep that file readable only by you:

install -m 600 /dev/null ~/.linxiv-web-password
printf '%s\n' 'your-password' > ~/.linxiv-web-password

A crontab entry that tags whatever arrived during the day, after the nightly import from bulk-import.md:

45 3 * * * cd $HOME/linxiv-web && LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_FILE=$HOME/.linxiv-web-password ./bulk-ai-tags.sh >> bulk-ai-tags-cron.log 2>&1

Five wrong passwords within five minutes lock out logins from that address for the rest of the five minutes (429 too many login attempts), so check the password file before you schedule it.

items.title: What to expect
items.text:
• Time: one AI call per paper, one at a time unless you pass --jobs. A cloud model takes a few seconds per paper. A local model in LM Studio or Ollama can take much longer, and the server waits up to 300 seconds for each answer from an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Try --dry-run for the count, then time the first few lines.
  • Cost and rate limits: with a cloud provider, every paper is one paid request. Free tiers often allow only a few requests per minute. When the provider answers with a rate-limit or overload error (429, 503 or 529), the script waits 30 seconds and tries that paper once more. If it fails again, the paper is logged as FAIL and picked up on the next run.
  • Vocabulary: the prompt lists up to 400 of the library's existing tags, and the model is told to reuse them. Tags added earlier in a run count as existing for the papers after them, so a library with no tags yet builds its vocabulary as the run goes. Look through the (new) tags in the log afterwards. The Tags page lists every tag with its paper count, which makes near-duplicates easy to spot.
  • Thin records: papers imported from scans or PDFs without embedded metadata often have only a stray title and no abstract, and get poor tags. Fix those first: in the Library, tick papers marked title?, open batch edit, and look them up (with "By PDF file name" when the file names are titles). See bulk-import.md.
  • Removing tags: the script only adds tags. To undo part of a run, remove the tags on the paper pages. The log lists every tag the script added, by paper.

Before tagging a large library, take a backup in Settings → Server & data → Backup.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Message Fix jq not found Install jq on the server: apt install jq cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:8086 The container is down, or the script isn't running on the server first-run setup is not done Open the web UI once and create the password login failed (401): invalid password Wrong password, or a stale LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_FILE login failed (429) Wait five minutes after repeated wrong passwords AI check failed (409): AI features are off Turn AI on in Settings → AI AI check failed (400): No … API key Add the provider's key in Settings → AI AI check failed (400): Choose a model Pick a model in Settings → AI and save AI check failed (400): Set the base URL … OpenAI-compatible provider: enter the endpoint's base URL in Settings → AI AI check failed (502): … request failed (ConnectError) The provider, or your local LM Studio or Ollama, can't be reached from the container FAIL … (502): … error 429 The provider's rate limit, still hit after the retry. Run again later, or use a plan with a higher limit FAIL … (502): … did not return valid JSON The model ignored the reply format. Pick a stronger model, or run again: replies vary FAIL … (404) The paper was deleted while the run was going

items.title: Importing a folder of PDFs on the server
items.text:
Use this when the PDFs are already on the machine that runs the linXiv-web container and you don't want to upload them one by one in the browser. scripts/bulk-import.sh runs on that machine and imports every PDF under a directory, subfolders included.

It has two modes:

Mode Container How it imports Use it when api (default) running uploads each file to POST /api/pdfs/import over 127.0.0.1 you want the library to stay online, or run imports from cron offline stopped runs linxiv pdf import in a one-off container, with the folder mounted read-only very large batches, files over the upload cap, or linking every paper to a project

Each PDF is imported the same way as Upload in the web UI: linXiv reads the metadata from the PDF and keeps its own copy in the PDF folder. --place changes that: move deletes each source file once it is imported, and in-situ leaves the files where they are and links each paper to its file. See Where the files end up. macOS ._* files are ignored.

Don't run docker exec linxiv-web linxiv pdf import ... while the container is up. linXiv allows one writing process per library, and the server can only keep its own calls in order. A second linxiv process writing next to it can fail or leave the library inconsistent. The script avoids this: api mode goes through the server, and offline mode only runs while the server is stopped.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• On the server: sh, curl, find, awk and sed (any Linux has them), and Docker Compose v2 for offline mode.
  • api mode: compose publishes the port on the server (the default 127.0.0.1:8086 works), and the admin password is set (first-run setup done, or LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH in .env).
  • offline mode: the PDFs must be readable by uid 1000, the user the container runs as.

items.title: Getting the script onto the server
items.text:
Copy it next to your docker-compose.yml:

scp scripts/bulk-import.sh server:linxiv-web/
ssh server 'chmod +x linxiv-web/bulk-import.sh'

Then, on the server:

cd linxiv-web
./bulk-import.sh --help

Check what it will pick up first:

./bulk-import.sh --dry-run /srv/inbox

items.title: api mode: container running
items.text:
./bulk-import.sh /srv/inbox

The script asks for the linXiv-web password, logs in, and uploads the files one at a time. You can keep using the web UI while it runs, though other requests wait their turn behind each import. Every file gets one line in the output and in the log file:

OK    2021/smith-rna.pdf -> doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2
FAIL  scans/notes.pdf (400): not a PDF file
done: 1 imported, 1 failed, 2 total. Log: ./bulk-import-20261008-221500.log

The exit status is 1 when any file fails, and 0 otherwise. DUP and SKIP lines (see Where the files end up) don't count as failures.

Options for this mode:

Option Effect --url URL Server address, if you changed LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT (default http://127.0.0.1:8086) --place copy\|move Keep the source files (default), or delete each one after it is imported --move-done DIR Move each imported file to DIR, keeping its subfolder. A rerun then only retries the failures --index-text After the imports, start the job that indexes PDF text for full-text search (the same as Index PDFs now in Settings → Library → PDF full text) --log FILE Log location (default ./bulk-import-<date>-<time>.log)

Run it on the server itself and point it at 127.0.0.1, not at a public HTTPS name. Over loopback, uploads skip the reverse proxy and its body size limit. The script also works when LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE=true.

items.title: Running it without a terminal (cron)
items.text:
The script reads the password from the first line of the file named in LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_FILE. Keep that file readable only by you:

install -m 600 /dev/null ~/.linxiv-web-password
printf '%s\n' 'your-password' > ~/.linxiv-web-password

A crontab entry that imports whatever lands in an inbox every night, and moves the imported files out of it:

15 3 * * * cd $HOME/linxiv-web && LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_FILE=$HOME/.linxiv-web-password ./bulk-import.sh --move-done /srv/inbox-done --index-text /srv/inbox >> bulk-import-cron.log 2>&1

Five wrong passwords within five minutes lock out logins from that address for the rest of the five minutes (429 too many login attempts), so check the password file before you schedule it.

items.title: offline mode: container stopped
items.text:
Stop the server, import, start it again:

docker compose stop linxiv-web
./bulk-import.sh --mode offline /srv/inbox
docker compose start linxiv-web

The script refuses to run while the container is up. It starts one container for the whole batch, with the same image, volumes and .env as the server, and mounts the folder read-only at /import. There is no login and no upload size cap, and it is faster than api mode because nothing goes over HTTP. Each file's result is written to the log as soon as it is done, so tail -f on the log shows how far a long run has got.

Options for this mode:

Option Effect --place copy\|move\|in-situ See Where the files end up (default copy) --project-id ID Link every imported paper to project ID (the number in the project's URL) --compose-dir DIR Folder that holds docker-compose.yml, if you run the script from elsewhere (default .) --service NAME Compose service name (default linxiv-web) --move-done DIR, --log FILE, --dry-run As in api mode

Full-text indexing needs the server, so after you start the container again, click Index PDFs now in Settings → Library → PDF full text.

On Linux, if every file fails with a permission error, give uid 1000 read access to the folder:

sudo chmod -R a+rX /srv/inbox

items.title: Where the files end up
items.text:
--place Modes Result copy (default) both linXiv stores its own copy, named after the paper id (doi_10.1016_j.cell.2026.08.035v1.pdf), at the top of the PDF folder. Your files stay where they are move both As copy, then each source file that imported is deleted. Files that failed stay, so a rerun only retries those in-situ offline No copy. Each paper points at its file where it is. For a collection that already lives in the PDF folder

in-situ only works on a folder inside the PDF folder (LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST, or a subfolder of it), because linXiv only opens PDFs from there. The script checks this and stops with an ABORT line otherwise. It imports each file, writes the file's own path into the library in place of linXiv's copy, and deletes the copy. This writes straight to papers.db, which is only safe while the server is stopped, so in-situ exists only in offline mode.

When two of your files turn out to be the same paper (same DOI or arXiv id), the first one keeps the link and the later one is reported as DUP and left on disk, unlinked. A copy linXiv made earlier, from a copy import or the web UI, doesn't count: your file replaces it and the copy is deleted. A file at the top of the PDF folder that is already named like one of linXiv's copies is reported as SKIP: importing it could overwrite the file with itself.

With in-situ, linXiv treats your files as its own:

  • Rename or move a file afterwards and its paper loses the PDF. Clean up file names before you import.
  • Settings → Library → PDF folders moves the files into its year and journal folders when you apply a layout.
  • Deleting a paper's PDF in linXiv deletes your file.
  • The storage total in Settings only counts files at the top of the PDF folder.

Running in-situ again on the same folder is safe: papers that already point at their files are left as they are. That includes a run that was interrupted. --dry-run shows the file list and the mode and placement it would use.

items.title: What to expect
items.text:
Running the script twice on the same files doesn't create duplicate papers. linXiv derives each paper's id from the arXiv id or DOI it finds in the PDF, or from a hash of the file (local:<hash>) when it finds neither, so a second import lands on the same paper and keeps any titles, authors or tags you edited since. Every file is still uploaded again, which is why --move-done speeds up repeated runs.

Metadata comes from the PDF alone. Scans and PDFs without embedded metadata get thin records: an empty title, a stray word such as "Abstract", or a DOI copied from a reference or a page footer, which gives the paper another article's metadata. The Library shows such papers with their file name instead of an empty title, and marks titles that look wrong, or unlike the file name, with title? and the file name underneath.

When your file names are the papers' titles (a Mendeley export, for example), fix them in batches: tick the flagged papers, open batch edit, pick Crossref or PubMed, tick "By PDF file name" and look them up. That search uses the title in each file name and ignores the stored DOI. The last candidate in each list is the file name itself, with the year folder as the date, for papers no source can find. A paper whose DOI was wrong keeps it as its id (for example doi:10.63485/...); the fix replaces its title, authors, date and DOI field.

In api mode, files over LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (default 200) fail with 413 file too large. Raise the variable in .env and run docker compose up -d, or import those files in offline mode. A single import that runs longer than LINXIV_WEB_TIMEOUT_LONG seconds (default 120) fails with a 504.

Before importing a large batch into an existing library, take a backup in Settings → Server & data → Backup.

items.text: Message Fix cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:8086 The container is down, or published on another port: pass --url first-run setup is not done Open the web UI once and create the password login failed (401): invalid password Wrong password, or a stale LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_FILE login failed (429) Wait five minutes after repeated wrong passwords FAIL ... (400): not a PDF file The file doesn't start with %PDF-: it is damaged, or not a PDF despite the extension FAIL ...: Could not extract PDF metadata (offline mode) Same as above: linXiv could not parse the file FAIL ... (paper already uses ...) Another file is the same paper. Keep one and delete the other, or ignore it --project-id is offline mode only The upload route has no project option. Use offline mode, or add the papers to the project in the web UI afterwards

items.title: Development
items.text:
Everything runs in containers.

# Server: ruff + pytest, including tests against the real linxiv and linxiv-mcp binaries
docker build --target server-test .

# Frontend: lint, type check, build
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/web":/w -w /w node:22-slim sh -c 'npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build'

# Just the CLI (handy for exploring its JSON output)
docker build --target cli -t linxiv-cli .
docker run --rm -v lxw-scratch:/data linxiv-cli stats

To build against a local linXiv checkout instead of a tag (its submodules must be initialised):

docker build --build-arg LINXIV_SRC=local --build-context linxiv-local=../linXiv .

The FastAPI server lives in server/. The CLI subprocess wrapper is app/cli.py, the AI provider client app/ai.py, and the MCP bridge app/mcp_bridge.py. The Vite, React and TypeScript frontend lives in web/. The Dockerfile builds the CLI and MCP server first, then the SPA, then the Python runtime image.

Branch and commit conventions match linXiv's; see CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository.

items.title: Running from a checkout
items.text:
cp .env.example .env
mkdir -p .dev/data .dev/pdfs

# Generate a password hash and paste it into .env (keep the single quotes)
docker compose build
docker compose run --rm --no-deps -e PASSWORD='your-password' linxiv-web python -m app hash-password

docker compose up -d

Open http://127.0.0.1:8086 and log in. After an update, rebuild and recreate the container (docker compose build && docker compose up -d --force-recreate), then reload the page with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R.

To keep the library elsewhere, set LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST and LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST in .env. Both directories must already exist. Keep the database directory on local disk, because SQLite over network or exFAT storage is unreliable.

For the prebuilt image, use Self-hosting instead.

items.title: This documentation site
items.text:
The site is built with Zensical, managed by uv from the repository root. Pages live in docs/, and zensical.toml holds the navigation.

uv sync                  # install Zensical into .venv
uv run zensical serve    # preview at http://localhost:8000, rebuilds on save
uv run zensical build    # write the static site to site/

site/ is ignored by git.

items.title: Functions not in the linxiv CLI
items.text:
What the web server provides that the linxiv CLI does not.

Compares the linxiv CLI that the web server wraps with the web server code in server/app/. Not an exhaustive diff.

items.title: Server-only code with no CLI command behind it
items.text:
• Auth: routes/auth.py has login, setup, logout and "me", plus the remember-me option (app/auth.py).
  • Knowledge graph: routes/graph.py builds the payload in Python, because the CLI has no graph command.
  • AI features: app/ai.py and routes/ai.py call Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic or a generic provider over httpx. They cover tag suggestions, summaries (saved as a note) and metadata cleanup, with write-only keys stored in settings.
  • MCP over HTTP at /mcp: app/mcp_bridge.py and routes/mcp.py run linxiv-mcp as a subprocess per session. It has a bearer token that is shown once, stored as a sha256 hash under web-only web_mcp_token_* keys, and can be rotated or revoked. The tool profile is read-only or read+write.
  • Background full-text worker: app/fulltext_worker.py runs as an asyncio task in the FastAPI lifespan. routes/sources.py exposes the job queue (/jobs, /jobs/{id}/cancel, /sources/worker, /sources/pending). The "Index now" button also goes through this.
  • PDF layout and folder moves: app/pdf_layout.py and app/pdf_text.py. Files are moved and PAPER_META.PDF_PATH is written straight into SQLite, because the CLI has no command to set a PDF location.
  • Direct external calls: PubMed via NCBI E-utilities (routes/metadata.py), and bioRxiv/medRxiv as a source (DOI-only, 2 MB cap).
  • POST /api/add: routes/add.py classifies the input (arXiv ID, DOI, publisher article link, PDF URL) on the server and then picks the CLI command. Publisher links (Nature, Springer, Wiley, ACS, APS, IOP, Science, PNAS and others) map to their DOI with the table from linXiv v0.7.0's recognize.rs, which only the linXiv app and linxiv-headless use. The publisher PDF is fetched on a best-effort basis: the server checks that the link returns a real PDF before linxiv pdf download stores it, because that command keeps whatever the link returns.
  • Metadata from the PDF's file name: app/pdf_name.py reads a title and a year folder from the stored PDF path. GET /papers and GET /papers/{id} flag titles that look like junk read from the PDF (title_suspect), and GET /papers/{id}/lookup?by=filename searches Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv or PubMed with the file name's title instead of the stored DOI.
  • PDF full text: routes/sources.py extracts a saved PDF's text with pypdf and stores it with linxiv paper set-text (linXiv v0.7.0). This works for one paper or as a job over every non-arXiv paper with a PDF. The CLI only fetches arXiv TeX source by itself.

items.title: Server-side logic layered on CLI results
items.text:
• Author merge candidates: name_candidates is computed on the server (exact full name, case-folded, minus ORCID matches and self). The CLI lacks this.
  • Author list filter: the "hide single-paper authors" filter runs server-side, because the CLI has no flag for it.
  • ORCID checks: format, orcid.org URL prefix stripped and check digit. The CLI stores any string.
  • Annotation anchors: validated with strict pydantic and re-serialized to {v,version,page,color,quote,rects}. The CLI stores any string.
  • Library search: local match plus paper search for queries of 3+ characters, merged. If the deep search fails, you get the plain hits plus an X-Deep-Search-Error header.
  • Project export: one GET /projects/{id}/export?format=… that streams the file back and uses the linXiv desktop app's slugified filename.
  • Project import: a stateless preview step, then a commit that re-uploads the file.
  • Upload endpoints: bibtex, zotero and PDF import take uploads instead of host paths.

items.title: Web UI features with no CLI or server counterpart
items.text:
• Search history in localStorage, honoring the shared search_history_enabled and _max settings, plus a "Clear search history" button the linXiv desktop app lacks.
  • Batch metadata edit, which reuses GET …/lookup and PUT …/metadata per paper, one at a time.
  • Crossref search tab (the CLI supports it, the linXiv desktop app doesn't) and a Query Builder for arXiv.
  • Zoom and density settings per browser.
  • Upload and Trash sidebar toggles that exist only in the web app.
  • Settings groups with #id deep links.

items.title: Blocked on the CLI
items.text:
These exist in linXiv, but only in the linxiv-headless HTTP API (linXiv docs/api.md), not in the CLI or linxiv-mcp (checked against v0.7.0). linXiv-web would need either new upstream CLI commands or linxiv-headless as its backend. The headless server cannot share the library with the CLI, because linXiv allows one process per library.

Feature linxiv-headless route linXiv-web today Per-paper reading status GET /api/reading-status, PUT /api/reading-status/{sid} Not available Link or unlink one paper and one author POST / DELETE /api/authors/{id}/papers/{pid} Merge whole authors only Change a highlight's anchor or color in place PATCH /api/annotations/{id} A color change deletes the highlight and creates a new one Clear a project's color PATCH /api/projects/{id} with color_hex: null Color can be set but not cleared Saved search state and history shared with the app GET / POST /api/search/state, GET /api/search/history History is kept per browser TeX diff between two versions of a paper GET /api/papers/{id}/full-text-diff Not available Backups taken before schema upgrades GET /api/storage/pre-migration-backups Not listed

items.title: MCP server
items.text:
linXiv-web can serve linXiv's own MCP tools over HTTP, so an AI agent such as Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode can search and work on your library. It is off by default.

Upstream linXiv ships linxiv-mcp as a local stdio server for the desktop app (see the linXiv README). linXiv-web builds the same binary and bridges it to MCP Streamable HTTP at /mcp, with a bearer token and a choice of which tools the agent gets.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
flowchart LR
  client[MCP client] -- "HTTP /mcp" --> api[FastAPI]
  api -- stdio --> mcpsrv[linxiv-mcp]
  mcpsrv --> data[("papers.db + pdfs/")]
  • Each MCP session (one initialize) gets its own linxiv-mcp process. At most 4 sessions run at once; a session closes after 30 minutes idle, and a restart of the container drops all sessions (clients re-initialize).
  • Requests in one session run one at a time. Replies are plain JSON; GET /mcp answers 405 (no server-sent events).
  • Which tools a client sees and may call is decided by the bridge (server/app/mcp_bridge.py), not by linxiv-mcp.

items.title: Turning it on
items.text:
1. Open Settings → Integrations.
  2. Tick Serve linXiv's MCP tools at /mcp and pick the tools the agent gets (see Profiles). Save.
  3. Click Create token. The token is shown once; only its SHA-256 is stored. Replace token or Revoke token disconnects every open session.

The card then shows the connect commands below with your server URL and token filled in.

items.title: Connecting a client
items.text: Use your server's address in place of http://127.0.0.1:8086, for example the HTTPS name behind your reverse proxy.

items.title: Claude Code
items.text:
claude mcp add --transport http linxiv http://127.0.0.1:8086/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Add --scope local (this project only, the default), --scope user (every project) or --scope project (writes .mcp.json into the repository, so keep the token out of git). Check with claude mcp list; the tools appear as mcp__linxiv__* after a restart or /mcp reconnect.

items.title: Codex
items.text:
Codex reads the token from an environment variable, which must be set in the shell that starts Codex:

export LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN=<token>
codex mcp add linxiv --url http://127.0.0.1:8086/mcp --bearer-token-env-var LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN

or in ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.linxiv]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8086/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN"

items.title: OpenCode
items.text:
Add a remote server to opencode.json (per project) or to your global OpenCode config. {env:LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN} reads the token from the environment, so set it as for Codex:

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "linxiv": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8086/mcp",
      "enabled": true,
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN}" }
    }
  }
}

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
Profile Tools Adds Read only (default) 32 search, get, list, refs, stats Read + edit library 68 papers, notes, tags, projects, highlights; soft deletes (to the trash) Full 75 hard deletes, merging papers or authors, metadata overwrite

Never exposed, in any profile:

  • get_settings, update_setting: the settings store holds API keys.
  • backup_database, restore_database, import_pdf, import_bibtex, import_zotero, import_project, export_project, export_project_bibtex, export_project_obsidian, export_project_zotero, set_full_text: they read or write file paths on the server. Use the web UI for these.

download_pdf with a caller-chosen url is refused; the paper's stored link is used, so the agent cannot make the server fetch an arbitrary host.

Tools added in a new upstream release stay hidden until they are classified in mcp_bridge.py (a test against the real binary fails on any unclassified tool).

items.title: Permission hints
items.text:
linxiv-mcp sets no MCP tool annotations, so the bridge adds them to every tool in tools/list, derived from the tool's profile tier. Clients use them to decide when to ask before a call.

Hint Set on readOnlyHint: true every Read only tool readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false Read + edit tools: changes you can undo (soft deletes go to the trash) destructiveHint: true Full tools: permanent deletes, merges, metadata overwrite idempotentHint: true edits that change nothing when repeated (adding/removing tags or project papers, restore, archive, create_tag) openWorldHint: true tools that call outside services (arXiv, DOI resolvers, feeds, ORCID sources) title readable name, e.g. List papers

Hints are advice to the client, not access control: the profile decides what can be called. A reasonable client setup is to auto-allow read-only tools and always confirm destructive ones by hand.

items.title: Tool reference
items.text: Descriptions come from linxiv-mcp (linXiv v0.7.0). Hints: read-only, edit (undoable), destructive (permanent), idempotent, open world (calls outside services).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• /mcp does not use the browser login or CSRF token. It needs Authorization: Bearer <token>; a missing or wrong token gets 401.
  • While the switch is off, /mcp answers 404.
  • A request carrying another site's Origin header is refused with 403, which blocks DNS-rebinding attacks from a browser.
  • Behind a reverse proxy, pass the Host header through (see self-hosting.md) so the Origin check compares against the public name.
  • Pick the smallest profile that does the job. Full lets an agent delete papers and projects permanently.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Probe the endpoint by hand. Streamable HTTP needs the Mcp-Session-Id returned by initialize on every later request:

URL=http://127.0.0.1:8086/mcp
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $LINXIV_MCP_TOKEN"
ACCEPT="Accept: application/json, text/event-stream"
CT="Content-Type: application/json"

SID=$(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "$URL" -H "$AUTH" -H "$ACCEPT" -H "$CT" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"0"}}}' \
  | tr -d '\r' | awk -F': ' 'tolower($1)=="mcp-session-id"{print $2}')

curl -s -X POST "$URL" -H "$AUTH" -H "$ACCEPT" -H "$CT" -H "Mcp-Session-Id: $SID" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}'

curl -s -X POST "$URL" -H "$AUTH" -H "$ACCEPT" -H "$CT" -H "Mcp-Session-Id: $SID" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  | jq -r '.result.tools[] | "\(.name)\t\(.annotations.readOnlyHint)\t\(.annotations.destructiveHint)"'
Reply Cause 404 on every request MCP switched off in Settings, or wrong path 401 Missing, wrong, replaced or revoked token 403 Request carries a different site's Origin 400 Missing Mcp-Session-Id Request after initialize without the session header 404 with a session id Session closed (idle, replaced token, restart); initialize again Tool not available on this server Tool is outside the chosen profile or always blocked

The current session count shows on the Settings card.

items.title: Self-hosting linXiv-web with Docker
items.text:
This guide runs linXiv-web on your own machine or home server from the prebuilt container image. For development and building from source, see Development.

The current release is the release branch, published as the image tag used below. main may contain changes that are not released yet.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Docker with Docker Compose v2 (docker compose), on Linux, macOS or Windows.
  • An amd64 or arm64 machine. The image is published for both.
  • Two directories on the host: one for the library database, one for PDFs.

The image bundles the linxiv CLI and linxiv-mcp, built from linXiv v0.7.0. Do not point linXiv-web at a data directory that the linXiv desktop app or linxiv-headless also uses: linXiv expects one process per library.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
mkdir -p linxiv-web/data linxiv-web/pdfs
cd linxiv-web

On Linux, the container runs as uid 1000 and must be able to write both directories:

sudo chown 1000:1000 data pdfs

Create docker-compose.yml:

services:
  linxiv-web:
    image: ghcr.io/toledoem/linxiv-web:0.1.2
    container_name: linxiv-web
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    ports:
      # 127.0.0.1 = this machine only. Use 0.0.0.0 to reach it from the LAN.
      - "${LINXIV_WEB_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT:-8086}:8000"
    volumes:
      # Long syntax: a missing host directory is an error, not a silently created empty one.
      - type: bind
        source: ${LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST:-./data}
        target: /data
        bind:
          create_host_path: false
      - type: bind
        source: ${LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST:-./pdfs}
        target: /pdfs
        bind:
          create_host_path: false
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health')"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

Start it:

docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f linxiv-web

Open http://127.0.0.1:8086.

The image is tagged with the linXiv-web version (0.1.2) and latest; pin the version to choose when you update. The image is public: no docker login needed.

items.title: First-run setup
items.text:
With no password configured, the server starts in setup mode and logs:

linxiv-web: no password set; first-run setup is open on 0.0.0.0:8000. The first visitor creates the admin password.

The first person to open the web UI creates the admin password (at least 8 characters) and is logged in. Until then every API call is refused. Do the setup before you publish the port to a network you don't trust.

After the password, the wizard offers optional steps, each with Skip:

  1. Contact emails for arXiv, Crossref and OpenAlex, and an NCBI (PubMed) API key.
  2. Theme and light/dark mode (stored in the browser).
  3. AI provider, model and key (off by default).
  4. Home feed URL and PDF folder layout.

Everything in the wizard can be changed later in Settings.

The password hash is stored in data/linxiv-web-auth.json (mode 0600). linXiv-web never stores the password itself.

items.title: Setting the password in .env instead
items.text:
A password from the environment always wins over the stored one, and setup never opens. Generate an argon2 hash:

docker run --rm -e PASSWORD='your-password' --entrypoint python \
  ghcr.io/toledoem/linxiv-web:0.1.2 -m app hash-password

Put it in .env next to docker-compose.yml, in single quotes (the hash contains $):

LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH='$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$...'

items.title: Changing or resetting the password
items.text:
Logged in: Settings → Server & data → Login changes the password and logs out every other browser. "Log out other sessions" there ends all sessions except yours.

Forgotten password: set a new one from the server, no restart needed (every browser is logged out):

docker compose exec linxiv-web python -m app reset-password

Or remove the stored password so the next visitor runs first-run setup again (the library is untouched):

docker compose down
rm data/linxiv-web-auth.json
docker compose up -d

A password set with LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH / LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD always wins; change it in .env instead.

items.title: Logging in
items.text:
Tick Remember me on this browser to stay logged in for 90 days (LINXIV_WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS changes this). Without it, the login ends when the browser closes, and after 14 days at most.

Sessions are kept in data/linxiv-web-state.db, so restarting or updating the container keeps you logged in.

items.title: Where your data lives
items.text:
Host directory Container Contents data/ (LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST) /data papers.db (library), user_settings.json (linXiv settings, including API keys entered in Settings), linxiv-web-auth.json (admin password hash), linxiv-web-state.db (sessions, login throttle) pdfs/ (LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST) /pdfs PDFs, flat or in year/journal subfolders (Settings → Library → PDF folders)

Keep data/ on a local disk: SQLite over network shares or exFAT is unreliable. pdfs/ may live on a NAS or external drive.

To use other locations, set them in .env (both directories must exist):

LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST=/srv/linxiv/data
LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST=/mnt/nas/papers

items.title: Reaching it from other machines
items.text:
Set in .env:

LINXIV_WEB_BIND=0.0.0.0
LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT=8086

then docker compose up -d, and open http://<server-ip>:8086. This is plain HTTP: use it on a trusted LAN, or put HTTPS in front.

items.title: HTTPS with a reverse proxy
items.text:
Keep LINXIV_WEB_BIND=127.0.0.1 and let the proxy on the same host forward to it. Set in .env:

LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE=true
LINXIV_WEB_HSTS=true   # optional: browsers stop using plain HTTP for this host

The proxy must pass the original Host header: linXiv-web rejects writes whose Origin doesn't match the host it sees.

linXiv-web serves only loopback, private LAN and link-local addresses unless LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true. Behind a proxy it sees the proxy's address, so everyone passes as the proxy. To see real client addresses, list the proxy in LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES (from inside the container it usually shows up as the Docker gateway, e.g. 172.17.0.1, or the whole 172.16.0.0/12) and make it send X-Forwarded-For; then internet clients need LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true.

Caddy (passes Host by default, gets certificates itself):

papers.example.org {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8086
}

nginx:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name papers.example.org;
    # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ...
    client_max_body_size 200m;   # match LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8086;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_read_timeout 300s;  # long searches, imports, AI calls
    }
}

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Settings changed in the web UI are stored in data/. Environment variables go in .env and need docker compose up -d to apply. The most useful ones:

Variable Default Purpose LINXIV_WEB_BIND / LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT 127.0.0.1 / 8086 Where compose publishes the port LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST / LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST ./data / ./pdfs Host directories LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH none Admin password hash; skips first-run setup LINXIV_WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS 90 Login lifetime with Remember me LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE false true behind HTTPS LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL false Serve public IP addresses (else 403) LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES none Proxy IPs/CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For is believed LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB 200 Upload size cap CROSSREF_MAILTO, NCBI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, … none Override the values entered in Settings

The full list is in Admin Server Configuration.

items.title: Importing many PDFs
items.text: To import a folder of PDFs that is already on the server, without the web UI, use scripts/bulk-import.sh. See bulk-import.md.

items.title: Backups
items.text:
• Database only: Settings → Server & data → Backup downloads a copy of papers.db and can import or restore one. It does not include PDFs.
  • Everything: stop the container and copy both directories:
docker compose down
tar czf linxiv-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz data pdfs
docker compose up -d

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Change the image tag in docker-compose.yml to the new version, then:

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Reload open browser tabs with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R so they pick up the new interface.

items.title: Building the image yourself
items.text:
Instead of pulling from GHCR, compose can build from the git repository. Replace the image: line with:

    build:
      context: https://github.com/ToledoEM/linXiv-web.git#release
      args:
        LINXIV_REF: v0.7.0
    image: linxiv-web:local

and run docker compose build && docker compose up -d. The first build compiles linXiv from source and takes several minutes. To build local changes, clone the repository and use context: ./linXiv-web instead of the URL.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Fix Container exits with LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR=/pdfs is not writable (or the data dir) On Linux: sudo chown 1000:1000 data pdfs ... does not exist (mount the PDF directory) Create the host directories before starting; compose won't create them Container exits with linxiv-web-auth.json is unreadable The stored password file is damaged: delete it and run setup again invalid password after setting LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH Keep the hash in single quotes in .env; compose expands $ otherwise Writes fail with cross-origin request rejected behind a proxy The proxy must forward the original Host header 403 External requests are disabled The client has a public IP address: set LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true, or reach it over LAN/VPN Container exits with LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES: '…' is not an IP or CIDR Use addresses or CIDRs, not host names Old interface after an update Hard reload with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R Logged out after a restart LINXIV_WEB_SECRET_KEY changed, or data/linxiv-web-state.db was deleted docker compose pull says denied Log in to ghcr.io (see Quick start)

items.title: Authors
items.text:
The Authors page lists every author in the library with their ORCID and paper count. Filter by name or ORCID, hide authors with a single paper, and sort by full name or last name.

An author page shows their papers. From there you can edit the full, first and last name and the ORCID, or merge the author with a duplicate. linXiv-web suggests merge candidates, including authors with the same name.

Settings → AI → Author ORCIDs fills in missing ORCIDs from Crossref and OpenAlex, 20 authors per click.

items.title: Knowledge graph
items.text:
The graph shows papers, authors and tags as nodes. Click a node to open it, and Ctrl/Cmd+click to select papers. The side panels adjust the layout forces and filter the graph by node type (papers, authors, tags), category, PDF, date range or tag.

With thousands of papers the graph gets dense and slow. Use filters to thin it out.

Export GraphML and Export CSV download the whole graph to rebuild it in another tool. GraphML opens in Gephi, Cytoscape, yEd, igraph and NetworkX. CSV is a zip with nodes.csv (id, type, label and metadata such as DOI, tags and projects) and edges.csv (source, target, type). The side-panel filters are not applied; Hide single-paper authors is.

items.title: Tags
items.text: The Tags page lists every tag with the number of papers that carry it, plus an Untagged row. Click a tag to open the Library filtered to it.

items.title: Home feed
items.text: The home page opens with library counts (papers, PDFs, PDF coverage, categories, tags) and then the home feed.

items.title: Feeds
items.text:
The feed shows entries from up to 10 RSS or Atom feeds, for example https://rss.arxiv.org/rss/cs.LG or a bioRxiv subject feed. Add, rename, switch off or remove feeds in Settings → Library → Home feed. The cache retention setting there controls how many days of feed entries stay stored; papers you dismiss for good are always remembered.

The picker above the list shows all feeds merged, a random 10 entries, or one feed at a time. The keyword box filters the list to entries that contain every one of the comma-separated keywords.

Save and Dismiss work on arXiv entries only.

items.title: Filter rules
items.text: Filter rules hide entries before you see them. A DENY rule hides an entry when all its comma-separated keywords appear in the chosen field (title or summary). An ALLOW rule overrides a DENY match. Rules apply to every feed and live in Settings → Library → Feed filters.

items.title: Saved PDFs view
items.text: Home also has a Saved PDFs view that lists 10 to 100 saved PDFs at random, by size, or only untagged ones.

items.title: Library
items.text: The Library lists every paper, 50 per page by default, with a page-size choice at the bottom.

items.title: Searching and filtering
items.text:
The search box covers title, abstract, authors, ids, tags, notes and indexed full text. A query of 3 or more characters also searches the TeX source and PDF text that linXiv has indexed. The chips above the table filter by PDF (All, Has PDF, No PDF) and the tag menu filters by one tag or by untagged papers.

Filters, sort order and page number are kept in the address bar, so a reload or the Back button returns to the same view, and you can bookmark it.

items.title: Sorting
items.text:
Click any column header (Title, Authors, Published, Category, Tags, PDF) to sort by it, and click again to reverse. The sort menu on the right does the same for the common orders.

In Settings → Appearance → Paper tables you can hide columns, change their widths, and show the DOI under each title.

items.title: Suspect titles
items.text: Papers imported from PDFs sometimes get a junk title read from the file. linXiv-web flags those with a title? pill and shows the PDF file name under the title, so you can tell which file the row came from. Fix them with metadata lookup on the paper page or in batch edit, using "Search by PDF file name" when the file names are real titles.

items.title: Batch edit
items.text:
Tick papers and open batch edit to:

  • look up and apply metadata from Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex, PubMed or bioRxiv/medRxiv, with a field diff before anything is saved;
  • add or remove tags, or ask the AI for tags if AI features are on;
  • export the selection as a .bib file.

While a batch runs, leaving the page asks for confirmation, because leaving stops the batch.

items.title: Dark mode
items.text: The theme follows your system setting until you pick light or dark with the toggle at the bottom of the sidebar or in Settings → Appearance.

items.title: Paper page
items.text: Each paper has its own page with metadata, abstract, tags, projects, notes, highlights and the PDF.

items.title: Metadata
items.text:
The top block shows id, version, publication date, categories, journal and link. Edit metadata opens an editor that can look the paper up in Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex, PubMed or bioRxiv/medRxiv and show the result next to the stored values. Pick the fields to take, then save. The default lookup source and which sources are on are set in Settings → Library → Metadata lookup.

A paper can be saved without authors; linXiv then stores the author as Unknown.

items.title: PDF reader
items.text:
View PDF opens the PDF to the right of the page. Drag the bar between the two panes to resize them; the width is remembered in your browser. Scrolling inside the PDF stays inside the PDF. On narrow screens the panes stack.

The reader has page navigation and find (Ctrl/Cmd+F or /). Select text to create a highlight. Open in new tab opens the file in the browser's own viewer. Delete PDF waits 5 seconds with an Undo button before it deletes.

items.title: Tags, projects and notes
items.text:
Add tags as a comma-separated list, or use AI Tags for suggestions when AI features are on. The Projects section adds the paper to an existing project or reading list, or creates a new one.

Notes are Markdown. Export .md saves the paper's notes for Obsidian. AI summary writes a summary from the abstract, or from the abstract plus PDF text, and saves it as a note when you ask.

items.title: Full text
items.text: For arXiv papers, Fetch TeX source downloads the LaTeX source and indexes its text for search. For other papers, Index PDF text indexes the PDF's text instead. A background worker can index all pending arXiv papers; see Settings.

items.title: Versions
items.text: arXiv version monitoring in Settings → Library checks saved arXiv papers for newer versions and lists each one with a link to the paper and a Dismiss button.

items.title: Projects
items.text:
The Projects page shows one card per active project, with its description and paper count. A switch shows archived projects instead, and deleted projects go to the Trash.

A project page lists its papers in the same sortable table as the Library. Add papers searches the library, and Export writes the project as:

  • .lxproj (optionally with PDFs), which another linXiv library can import;
  • BibTeX;
  • an Obsidian vault;
  • Zotero;
  • notes as a Markdown .zip.

Import... on the Projects page reads a .lxproj file. It shows a preview first and asks whether to merge with or overwrite a project of the same name.

items.title: Reading lists
items.text:
A reading list is a project tagged reading-list. Reading lists have their own page and stay off the Projects page. Open one to add papers.

linXiv keeps a per-paper reading status (unread, reading, read) only in its linxiv-headless HTTP API, not in the CLI, so linXiv-web can't show it yet. See Functions not in the CLI.

items.title: Search
items.text:
The Search page has tabs for arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref and your local library. Pick how many results you want and the sort order, then search.

Advanced opens an arXiv query builder: each clause searches all fields, title, author or abstract, and clauses combine with AND, OR or AND NOT. Results already in your library link to their paper page.

items.title: Add paper
items.text:
The Add paper page has three sections.

Add by link or identifier Paste an arXiv link or id, a DOI or doi.org link, a publisher article link (Nature, Springer, Wiley, ACS, APS, IOP, Science, PNAS and others), or a direct link to a PDF. For a PDF link the server downloads the file itself, from public hosts only and up to the upload size cap. Upload PDF files Drop PDFs or choose them. linXiv reads the metadata from each PDF and adds the paper with its PDF. Import a metadata file A BibTeX .bib file or a Zotero CSL JSON export. Only metadata is imported, no PDFs. Entries already in the library are updated, and papers in the trash are restored.

To import a whole folder of PDFs that is already on the server, use the bulk import script.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Settings are split into groups listed on the left. Each card has its own Save button. You can link to a group directly, for example /settings#ai.

Settings marked as stored in the browser (theme, zoom, density, sidebar pages, paper table columns) apply to that browser only. Everything else is stored on the server.

items.title: Appearance
items.text: Theme, light/dark/system mode, zoom and density. Display turns TeX rendering in titles and abstracts on or off. Sidebar picks which pages appear in the sidebar; Home, Library, Projects, Authors and Settings always do. Paper tables sets the visible columns, their widths and where the DOI is shown.

items.title: Library
items.text:
• Home feed: the feeds on the home page and how long entries are kept. See Home feed.
  • Feed filters: DENY and ALLOW rules for feed entries.
  • Search: whether search terms are saved for autocomplete, and how many.
  • Metadata lookup: which sources are on and the default one.
  • Contacts & API keys: contact addresses sent to arXiv, Crossref and OpenAlex, and the NCBI key for PubMed. Values set as environment variables take precedence.
  • Full-text index: the background worker that fetches and indexes TeX source for saved arXiv papers.
  • PDF full text: indexes PDF text for papers without TeX source.
  • arXiv version monitoring: checks saved arXiv papers for newer versions.
  • PDF folders: arranges the PDF folder by year, journal, or both, with a preview before any file moves.

items.title: Server & data
items.text: Storage sets a cap on total PDF size; downloads and imports stop once saved PDFs reach it. Login changes the password and can log out every other session. Backup downloads, imports or restores the database. Logs shows the server log, and Activity lists every change made through the API.

items.title: AI
items.text:
Switch AI features on, choose a provider, model and key, and test the connection. Author ORCIDs fills in missing ORCIDs. See AI features.

API keys are write-only. After saving, the page shows only their last 4 characters.

items.title: Integrations
items.text: The MCP server for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode: switch it on, choose the tool profile and create the access token. See MCP server.

items.title: About
items.text: Version, update check against the published image (by hand or daily, weekly or monthly), health warnings about the configuration, disk space used by the data, PDF and log folders, and a diagnostics report for bug reports.

items.title: Trash
items.text:
Deleting a paper or project moves it to the Trash. Deleted papers stay there until you restore them or delete them forever, and a restored paper comes back with its PDF and project links. Deleted projects are listed below the papers and can be restored the same way.

Delete forever asks you to confirm and cannot be undone.

items.title: Backups
items.text:
Settings → Server & data → Backup has three actions:

  • Download a backup: a snapshot of the database (papers, metadata, tags, projects, notes and authors). Saved PDF files are not included.
  • Import: merges another linXiv database into this library.
  • Restore: replaces the library with the backup. It is refused while a background job runs.

Back up the PDF folder separately. Self-hosting shows which folders to copy.

items.title: HTTP API
items.text:
The web UI uses this API, and scripts can call it too. Every route except /api/health, /api/login, /api/me and /mcp needs a session when a password is set. Write requests also need the X-CSRF-Token header, which echoes the lxw_csrf cookie.

Most routes map to one linxiv CLI command. The right column names the command or describes what the server does.

Route linxiv command / behaviour POST /api/password {current, new, remember?} Change the stored admin password (409 when it comes from LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD(_HASH)); logs out every other session POST /api/sessions/revoke-others Log out every session except the caller's; returns {revoked} GET /api/activity?limit, GET /api/activity/export Activity log, newest first / as CSV: every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE under /api/ with time, client address, route, path parameters, status (Settings saves: key names only). Kept in <data dir>/logs/activity.jsonl, 5 MiB + one rotated file DELETE /api/activity {confirm: "delete activity log"} Clear the activity log (the clear is recorded) GET /api/system/diagnostics Markdown report for bug reports: versions, configuration, library counts, disk, health, running jobs, DNS + TCP 443 reachability of outside services. Secrets and addresses that could locate the server only as set / not set GET /api/search?q&source=arxiv\|openalex\|crossref&max search POST /api/papers/{id}/fetch?source= fetch, then paper get GET /api/papers?q&tag&pdf=has\|none&fulltext&limit&offset&category&sort&dir list filtered server-side; a q of 3+ characters also runs paper search (TeX full text and notes), hits flagged deep_match; fulltext=true returns only the paper search hits. Each paper also gets pdf_file (its PDF's path inside the PDF folder) and title_suspect (the title looks like junk read from the PDF, or unlike the file name) GET /api/papers/{id}, GET /api/papers/{id}/versions paper get (plus pdf_file and title_suspect), paper versions DELETE /api/papers/{id} paper delete (soft delete, goes to trash) GET /api/papers/{id}/pdf pdf path, then serves the file (only from inside the data or PDF dir) POST /api/papers/{id}/pdf {url?, version?} pdf download (for arXiv papers the URL is derived) DELETE /api/papers/{id}/pdf pdf delete PUT /api/papers/{id}/metadata {title, authors[], published, summary, category?, doi?, url?} paper get, then paper repair with the full record and the paper's current tags (repair clears any field it isn't given) GET /api/papers/{id}/lookup?source=crossref\|arxiv\|openalex\|pubmed\|biorxiv&by=auto\|filename Candidate metadata: doi resolve (by DOI), search (by arXiv id or title), NCBI E-utilities for PubMed (by DOI, then title), api.biorxiv.org (by DOI). by=filename searches by the title in the PDF's file name, ignoring the stored DOI, and adds a last candidate built from the file name and its year folder GET/POST/DELETE /api/papers/{id}/tags tag list / tag add / tag remove GET /api/pdfs, GET /api/pdfs/storage pdf list, pdf storage (recounted including subfolders) POST /api/pdfs/import (multipart file) pdf import GET /api/pdfs/layout/preview?layout=, POST /api/jobs/pdf-layout PDF folder layout (none, year, journal, year/journal, journal/year): preview, then a job that moves files and updates their stored path POST /api/import/bibtex, POST /api/import/zotero (multipart file) bibtex import, zotero import (upsert: existing entries are updated) POST /api/add {input} arXiv id/link: fetch; DOI or doi.org link: doi save; other http(s) link: server downloads the PDF (public hosts only, size-capped), then pdf import GET /api/stats, /api/categories, /api/tags stats, categories, tag list-all GET /api/authors?hide_single, GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/authors/{id} author list, author get, author update, author delete (409 while linked to papers) GET /api/authors/{id}/merge-candidates, POST /api/authors/{id}/merge author merge-candidates (plus same-name hints), author merge POST /api/orcid/backfill {limit?} orcid backfill (1 to 100; 409 while one runs) GET /api/projects?status=active\|archived, POST /api/projects, PATCH /api/projects/{id} project list, project create, project update GET /api/projects/{id}, GET /api/projects/{id}/papers project get; papers = project get + list, filtered to members in project order POST /api/projects/{id}/papers ({"source_ids": [...]}), DELETE /api/projects/{id}/papers/{source_id} project add-papers (200 with added/failed), project remove-paper GET /api/projects/{id}/export?format=lxproj\|bibtex\|obsidian\|zotero&pdfs project export [--pdfs], export-bibtex, export-obsidian, export-zotero; written to a temp dir, sent as a download, then deleted POST /api/projects/import/preview, POST /api/projects/import (multipart file, on_conflict=merge\|overwrite) project import --preview, project import (.lxproj, zip checked before the CLI sees it) POST /api/projects/{id}/archive, POST /api/projects/{id}/restore, DELETE /api/projects/{id} project archive, project restore, project delete (soft delete, goes to trash) GET /api/notes?paper=&project=, POST /api/notes, PATCH /api/notes/{id}, DELETE /api/notes/{id} note list, note create [--project-id], note update, note delete (permanent); title/content capped at 100 kB GET /api/annotations?paper=&project=, POST /api/annotations, PATCH /api/annotations/{id}, DELETE /api/annotations/{id} annotation list/create/update/delete (PDF highlights; anchors validated server-side) GET /api/graph Knowledge graph of papers, authors and tags, built from list and author list GET /api/graph/export The same graph as a file: format=graphml (default) or format=csv (zip of nodes.csv and edges.csv); exclude_single_authors=true drops single-paper authors GET /api/feed, POST /api/feed/dismiss feed get for the stored home feed URL (cached 5 minutes), feed dismiss GET /api/feed/rules, POST /api/feed/rules, DELETE /api/feed/rules/{id} feed rules list/add/delete GET /api/versions/new, POST /api/versions/check {limit?}, POST /api/versions/{id}/ack versions new, versions check --limit (1 to 100, default 20; stores new versions it finds), versions ack (a second ack still returns ok) POST /api/papers/{id}/source {force?} paper fetch-source [--force]: downloads the paper's arXiv LaTeX source and indexes its text for full-text search (400 for non-arXiv papers) GET /api/sources/pending, GET /api/sources/worker Saved arXiv papers whose source isn't indexed; status of the background full-text indexer POST /api/jobs/index-sources {limit?}, GET /api/jobs?kind=, GET /api/jobs/{id}, POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel Background job: one paper fetch-source per pending paper, 7 s apart (409 if one is already running) GET /api/trash trash list POST /api/trash/papers/{id}/restore, DELETE /api/trash/papers/{id} trash restore, trash hard-delete (paper must be in the trash) POST /api/trash/projects/{id}/restore, DELETE /api/trash/projects/{id} trash restore-project, trash hard-delete-project GET /api/backup, POST /api/backup/import, POST /api/backup/restore (multipart file) backup (database snapshot download), import (merge another database), restore (replace the library; refused while a job runs) GET /api/settings, PATCH /api/settings settings get, settings update, limited to an allowlist (storage cap, TeX rendering, contact addresses, home feed, search history, full-text worker, AI and MCP settings); API keys are write-only GET /api/ai/models, POST /api/ai/test, GET /api/ai/schemas Provider model list, connection test, the JSON Schema and example each AI action uses (409 while AI is off) POST /api/ai/tags/{id}, POST /api/ai/summary/{id}?pdf=, POST /api/ai/cleanup/{id} AI tag suggestions, summary, metadata cleanup; previews only, nothing is written GET /api/mcp, POST /api/mcp/token, DELETE /api/mcp/token MCP status, create (shown once) or revoke the access token POST/GET/DELETE /mcp MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint (bearer token; see MCP server)

Paper ids are linXiv source ids such as arxiv:1706.03762. Old-style arXiv ids keep their slash: /api/papers/arxiv:hep-th/9901001.

items.title: linXiv versions
items.text:
linXiv-web linXiv CLI / MCP 0.1.x v0.7.0

The image builds linxiv and linxiv-mcp from upstream source at the LINXIV_REF build arg (default v0.7.0).

items.title: Resource usage
items.text:
Measured on a home server (Intel i7-7560U, 4 threads, 16 GB RAM) with a library of about 6,000 papers, 6,000 PDFs and 2,000 tags:

Image size 357 MB on disk (91 MB compressed) Memory, idle 155–185 MiB Memory, peak 302 MiB CPU, idle under 1% Data dir (papers.db, logs, state) 16 MB PDFs 12 GB (on a separate USB disk)

No CPU or memory limits were set.

items.title: Bare metal requirements
items.text:
Not supported, but feasible without code changes. Docker is the tested path. Running directly on a host needs:

  • linxiv and linxiv-mcp built from the linXiv repo at v0.7.0 (Rust toolchain, cargo build --release -p linxiv-cli -p linxiv-mcp), on PATH or set with LINXIV_BIN / LINXIV_MCP_BIN
  • PDFium library from linXiv's scripts/fetch_pdfium.sh, with LINXIV_PDFIUM_LIB set to its path
  • Python 3.11+ and uv for the server (cd server && uv sync --frozen --no-dev)
  • Node.js and npm to build the web UI once (cd web && npm ci && npm run build), with LINXIV_WEB_STATIC_DIR set to web/dist
  • Data and PDF directories, with LINXIV_DATA_DIR and LINXIV_WEB_DATA_DIR set to the same path, plus LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR
  • <data dir>/pdfs linked to the PDF directory, as entrypoint.sh does in the container
  • LINXIV_WEB_HOST set for network access (the default is 127.0.0.1)
  • A service manager (systemd, launchd) to run python -m app as a non-root user and restart it

items.title: PDF folder on an SMB share
items.text:
Not tested on SMB, but the design allows it. Only the data dir must stay on a local disk.

Key points:

  • Ownership: the container runs as uid 1000 and CIFS ignores chown. Mount with uid=1000,gid=1000,file_mode=0644,dir_mode=0755.
  • Mount the share on the host (/etc/fstab or systemd, with _netdev,nofail) and bind-mount it as /pdfs, rather than using Docker's CIFS volume driver.
  • Start order: the server refuses to start when the PDF folder is missing, which stops writes into an empty mount point. Start the container after the mount, for example with x-systemd.automount.
  • Share offline: if the NAS sleeps or the network drops, PDF reads, imports and downloads fail, and on a hard mount they can hang until LINXIV_WEB_TIMEOUT_LONG (120 s). Library data is not affected.
  • Speed: opening PDFs, the full-text indexer and layout moves run at network speed. The rest of the app does not touch the PDF folder.
  • File names: with the "by journal" layout, SMB may reject or change characters in journal names that a Linux filesystem accepts.

items.title: Admin Server Configuration
items.text:
linXiv-web reads these environment variables, usually from the .env file next to docker-compose.yml.

Variable Default Purpose LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD_HASH none argon2 hash of the login password (python -m app hash-password). Without it (or LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD), first-run setup in the browser creates the password, stored in <data dir>/linxiv-web-auth.json LINXIV_WEB_PASSWORD none Plain password, hashed in memory at startup (dev only) LINXIV_WEB_SECRET_KEY generated, kept in <data dir>/linxiv-web-state.db Session signing key. Changing it logs everyone out LINXIV_WEB_COOKIE_SECURE false Set to true behind HTTPS LINXIV_WEB_HSTS false Send Strict-Transport-Security (1 year). Only behind HTTPS: browsers then refuse plain HTTP to this host LINXIV_WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS 90 Login lifetime when "Remember me" is ticked (otherwise the login lasts until the browser closes, at most 14 days) LINXIV_WEB_DATA_DIR /data linXiv data dir (papers.db). Passed to the CLI and MCP server as LINXIV_DATA_DIR LINXIV_WEB_PDF_DIR /pdfs PDF directory, symlinked from <data dir>/pdfs LINXIV_WEB_HOST / LINXIV_WEB_PORT 0.0.0.0 / 8000 in the image Listen address LINXIV_WEB_ALLOW_EXTERNAL false Serve clients with public IP addresses. Off: only loopback, private LAN and link-local clients get through (others get 403) LINXIV_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXIES none Comma-separated IPs/CIDRs of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is believed (read right to left). Unlisted proxies count as the client LINXIV_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_MB 200 Upload size cap LINXIV_WEB_TIMEOUT_LONG / _SHORT 120 / 30 CLI timeout in seconds (search, fetch, download and import use the long one) LINXIV_BIN / LINXIV_MCP_BIN linxiv / linxiv-mcp CLI and MCP server binaries ARXIV_MAILTO, CROSSREF_MAILTO, OPENALEX_MAILTO none Contact addresses sent to those services; override the values set in Settings NCBI_API_KEY none PubMed key; overrides the one set in Settings GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GENAI_API_KEY_TAG_GEN none AI provider keys (the last one is for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint); override the ones set in Settings LINXIV_WEB_AI_ALLOWED_HOSTS none Comma-separated host names the OpenAI-compatible base URL may use. Unset: any host except cloud metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fd00:ec2::254, 100.100.100.200), which are always refused

Keys entered in Settings are stored in the linXiv settings store. The server never sends them back to the browser, only their last 4 characters.

The Compose file also reads LINXIV_WEB_BIND, LINXIV_WEB_PUBLISH_PORT, LINXIV_WEB_DATA_HOST and LINXIV_WEB_PDF_HOST to decide where the port is published and which host folders are mounted. Self-hosting explains them.
